cognate: *ph₂tḗr (πατήρ ~ pitā́) and *méh₂tēr (μήτηρ ~ mātā́) as the predicates of Sky and Earth respectively; Ved. dyaúḥ < *dyḗws (cognate with Ζεύς, Iu-ppiter) and pṛthivī́ < *pl̥th₂éwih₂ in the Indic witnesses.
drift_or_renewal: Both cosmic nouns are renewed in Greek: Sky *dyḗws → οὐρανός (Pindar O. 7.38 Οὐρανός … Γαῖα μάτηρ; Aristotle οὐρανὸν … πατέρας), Earth *pl̥th₂éwih₂ → γῆ/γαῖα (the old word survives only as a name). The father member is also renewed inside Indic: AVŚ 12.1 has parjanyaḥ pitā (the rain-cloud as father), exactly paralleling the Greek and Latin rationalisations in which the father is the sky/sun that sends seed or rain (Aristotle οὐρανὸν καὶ ἥλιον … ὡς γεννῶντας; Lucretius caelesti semine … Pater, umoris guttas … Mater terra). The kin terms stay cognate throughout.
shared_syntax: Paired nominal predications/appositions: [Sky] (is) father, [Earth] (is) mother, often as a balanced pair in one clause (dyauṣ pitā pṛthivī mātā; τὴν γῆς φύσιν ὡς … μητέρα … οὐρανὸν … πατέρας) and as a vocative pair (RV 6.51.5 dyaùṣ pítaḥ pŕ̥thivi mā́tar ~ Greek ὦ γαῖα μῆτερ / Ζεῦ πάτερ).
context: Cosmogonic/genealogical: Earth as the mother who bears and feeds all beings (AVŚ 12.1 Pṛthivī hymn; AVŚ 3.23 plants whose father is Sky and mother Earth; Plato Menex. 237e earth as mother who bore men; Hes. Op. 563 γῆ πάντων μήτηρ), Sky as begetting father. Aristotle reports it as what people commonly say (νομίζουσιν … προσαγορεύουσιν), i.e. traditional diction, not his invention. Not chance: the specific assignment Sky=father / Earth=mother in a fixed pair, with *dyḗws *ph₂tḗr itself surviving as a compound/vocative in Greek and Latin (Ζεῦ πάτερ, Iuppiter, Diespiter) — a textbook inherited theonym-formula.

cognate: Both members: waking = reduplicated *h₁ge-h₁gor- (Gk perf. ἐγρήγορα, ptc. ἐγρηγορώς ~ Ved. jāgṛ-/jāgāra, ptc. jāgrat-); sleeping = *swep-/*sup-no- (ὕπνος ~ svap-, svápna-).
drift_or_renewal: In Greek the sleep member is usually renewed with εὕδω/καθεύδω (Heraclitus, Plato Symp., Leges), and the nominal ἐν ὕπνῳ replaces a participle in Rep. 476c; the waking member keeps the old reduplicated perfect in both branches.
shared_syntax: Disjunctive merism of two participial states with a doubled conditional/relative particle: ἐάν τε ἐν ὕπνῳ τις ἐάν τ’ ἐγρηγορώς ~ yadi jāgrad yadi svapan (AVŚ 6.115), jāgrato yat svapantaḥ (RV 10.164.3), 'whether waking or sleeping', meaning 'at all times / in every state'.
context: Indic: expiation formulas for sin committed in either state (enas, duṣkṛta); Greek: Plato on whether one 'dreams' in either state. The congruence is only in the merism and its frame (an all-states quantifier), not in the ritual setting; Rep. 330e (B-71a6a, the wrongdoer starting up from sleep in fear) gives a guilt context but is not itself the merism.

note: All 173 bundles read. Most pair Plato/Aristotle/Hippocratic prose with Cato agr./Lucretius/AV and are vocabulary-only. Two claims: Sky-father/Earth-mother (medium, recalled) and the waking/sleeping merism (low). Considered and rejected: ἐσθὴς ποικίλη ~ piśáṅgā vasate (default words, incongruent contexts; the better Gk-Av match h.Ven. 86 ~ Yt 13.3 has no slab anchor); νύμφη νέη ~ noua nupta (single Greek instance); Pl. Rep. 621a ~ ORV lav 192.9 water-by-measure (Byzantine ascetic topos, contact not inheritance); κύνες/λύκοι ~ canes/lupi (incongruent).
